newsitem.title: UK: British campaign wants more joy for toy workers.
newsitem.headline: British campaign wants more joy for toy workers.

text.p: A British Third-World campaign group on Wednesday urged Christmas shoppers to buy "people friendly" toys, saying workers making some of the world's top selling toys often worked long hours in poor conditions.
The World Development Movement (WDM) said in a report that Britons spend as much on toys for one child at Christmas as a Chinese toy worker earns in three months.

"The best present toy companies could give their workers this Christmas is safe working conditions. Toy companies should listen to the thousands of Christmas shoppers who want to buy "people friendly' toys," said the WDM.
Most of the toys that will be bought in the West this Christmas are made in factories in Asia, where most labourers work long hours often in dilapidated and unsafe buildings, the report said.

"An average working day lasts eleven or twelve hours usually six or seven days a week with no holidays. Many workers have to do overtime just to earn enough to support their families," the WDM report said.
Many international toy manufacturers and retailers have already adopted safety codes to improve conditions in factories.
The WDM said better monitoring was needed to enforce codes.

"WDM believes that by adopting a code, toy companies demonstrated their concerns with every toy purchase. By agreeing to develop independent monitoring, they could translate the concern into real improvements," it said.
